context_chunks.text: Minor keying error. Treat as a paid parking event with a registration mismatch and apply the applicable Code/keying-error requirements. Keying and payment are one case theory - do not repeat.

The discrepancy concerns a minor registration-entry error. Payment was nevertheless made. The operator should match the transaction and deal with the case in accordance with the applicable current keying-error requirements.
Multiple visits / double visit. Require review of the complete ANPR sequence rather than two selected images. Keeper-safe - 'the vehicle attended on more than one occasion'.
Payment made. Lead with payment and require the operator to reconcile its transaction records with the parking event. Merge repeated payment statements into one.

The allegation that the applicable parking tariff was not paid is disputed. A payment was made in connection with the vehicle's use of the site. The operator should review its payment records against the parking event before continuing enforcement.
Notwithstanding the registration-entry error, the applicable tariff was paid. The case should not be treated as though the parking facility was used without payment.

The operator is requested to conduct a reasonable search of its payment records for the relevant location and period, including transactions capable of being matched to the parking event rather than relying solely on an immediate VRM match.

The vehicle attended the location on more than one separate occasion. The first recorded entry and final recorded exit must not be treated as one continuous parking event without review of the complete sequence.
The operator should review the complete sequence of captures for the vehicle and date, including intermediate entry/exit records, rather than relying only on the two images reproduced on the PCN.

actual.letter:
I write as the registered keeper of vehicle AB12CDE in respect of Parking Charge Notice FS689271. I dispute liability for this parking charge and require the operator to consider this appeal.

The Parking Charge Notice alleges: Overstayed paid time at Fieldstone Retail.

The allegation that the applicable parking tariff was not paid is disputed. A payment was made in connection with the vehicle's use of the site. The operator should review its payment records against the parking event before continuing enforcement. The operator is requested to conduct a reasonable search of its payment records for the relevant location and period, including transactions capable of being matched to the parking event rather than relying solely on an immediate VRM match. The discrepancy concerns a minor registration-entry error. The operator should match the transaction and deal with the case in accordance with the applicable current keying-error requirements. The case should not be treated as though the parking facility was used without payment.

The vehicle attended the location on more than one separate occasion. The first recorded entry and final recorded exit must not be treated as one continuous parking event without review of the complete sequence.

The operator should review the complete sequence of captures for the vehicle and date, including intermediate entry/exit records, rather than relying only on the two images reproduced on the PCN.

For the reasons set out above, the parking charge is disputed and the operator is requested to cancel the Parking Charge Notice.
